preference_reason: B better connects the recommendation to the runbook's deployment sequence and gives a more proportionate review, while A omits rolling compatibility and elevates secondary concerns into mandatory changes.

skill.notes: “Only changes metadata, so it is fast” identifies the migration's concrete benefit, but the response never addresses migrations preceding the rolling deploy or old-version compatibility. It correctly labels MEDIUM and separates “Verified” facts from the “unverified” Postgres version, although mandatory lock-timeout and list-payload changes overemphasize secondary concerns. “Plan status: REVIEWED” and “Approve the plan with changes 1–3 applied? yes/no” preserve the approval boundary and provide a concrete next step; repeated sections make the review unnecessarily long.

baseline.notes: “CI runs the migration before the rolling deploy” and “Old replicas ... keep working” identify deployment compatibility and its consequence. The migration discussion cites the DEFAULT incident and recommended shape, but never explicitly establishes that this change is metadata-only and avoids rewriting 41M rows. The statement that automatic return is “only true for detail” contradicts its own observation that the list also returns notes; implementation choices such as trimming add unnecessary decisions. “I didn't change or run anything” establishes review-only activity, but there is no explicit approval checkpoint.
